class.name: AttributeSet
class.brief_description: Resource holding named numeric attributes and their derived current values.
class.description: Base values are authored in the editor as a name to value dictionary; current values are derived at runtime from the base plus every active modifier. The formula is [code](base + sum of ADD) * product of MULTIPLY[/code], and a single [code]OVERRIDE[/code] wins over all of it. Override [code]_pre_attribute_change[/code] to clamp a value before it is written, and [code]_post_attribute_change[/code] to react after it is. From C#, connect to the signals instead - C# cannot inherit GDExtension classes. [b]A [code].tres[/code] holding a subclass of this must declare that type in its header[/b] - [code][lb]gd_resource type="AttributeSet" script_class="MyAttributes" ...[rb][/code], not [code]type="Resource"[/code]. Godot will not attach a script whose base is a GDExtension class to a resource declared as something else; the file then loads as a plain [Resource] with no script and no attributes, silently. The editor writes the correct header itself, so this only bites a hand-written or hand-edited file. [b]Attributes do not exist until [AbilitySystemComponent] is ready[/b], which is when it duplicates this template and calls [method init_current_from_base]. Anything whose [code]_ready[/code] runs earlier - a sibling, a child of the pawn root, a HUD - reads [code]0.0[/code] with no warning. Read attributes at the point of use, and choose a fallback that means "not configured" rather than one that means "do nothing": for a multiplier that is [code]1.0[/code], never [code]0.0[/code].

method.name: _post_attribute_change
method.description: Override to react to a change that has already been written - death at zero health, a derived stat that follows another. From C#, connect to [signal attribute_changed] instead: a GDExtension virtual cannot be overridden there.

method.name: _pre_attribute_change
method.description: Override to clamp. [b]Return the value to actually store[/b] - this is the hook where [code]health[/code] gets held between zero and [code]max_health[/code]. Called before the change is written, so [method get_current_value] still reads the old one.

method.name: define_attribute
method.description: Declares [param attribute_name] with [param base_value]. Use it to build a set from code; authored sets fill [member attributes] in the inspector instead.

method.name: get_base_value
method.description: The authored value, before any modifier.

method.name: get_current_value
method.description: The value after modifiers: [code](base + sum of ADD) * product of MULTIPLY[/code], with a single [constant AttributeModifier.OVERRIDE] beating all of it. Falls back to the base value until [method init_current_from_base] has run.

method.name: has_attribute
method.description: Whether [param attribute_name] is defined. An undefined attribute reads as [code]0.0[/code] rather than failing, so check this when zero is a meaningful value.

method.name: init_current_from_base
method.description: Resets every current value to its base, discarding what modifiers had computed.

method.name: set_base_value
method.description: Sets the authored value and emits [signal base_value_changed]. This is the one a permanent change writes to - a level-up, a purchased upgrade - while temporary changes belong in a [GameplayEffect].

method.name: set_current_value
method.description: Writes the derived value, passing it through [method _pre_attribute_change] first, then emitting [signal attribute_changed] and calling [method _post_attribute_change]. Setting it to what it already holds does nothing.

members.member: The authored base values, as name to number. This is the template on disk: [AbilitySystemComponent] duplicates the set at runtime, so play never mutates the resource.

signal.name: attribute_changed
signal.description: A current value changed, after modifiers. This is what UI should listen to.

signal.name: base_value_changed
signal.description: An authored value changed. Fires for a permanent change, not for a [GameplayEffect] modifying the current value.
